quests.question: Each employee ___ a badge to enter the building.
quests.hint: 'Each' looks at one member of the group at a time, so treat it like a singular subject.
quests.explanation: 'Each employee' refers to one person at a time, even though there are many employees overall. Singular subjects like this need the -s ending: 'needs'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Each apartment in this complex ___ its own parking space.
quests.hint: 'Each apartment' still means one apartment at a time - ignore the phrase describing the building.
quests.explanation: 'Each apartment' is singular, and 'in this complex' is just extra detail. Singular subjects take 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Each child ___ a chance to ask questions after the lesson.
quests.hint: 'Each child' zooms in on one child at a time, so the verb should match a singular subject.
quests.explanation: 'Each child' is singular, so the verb takes the -s ending: 'gets'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' + singular noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Every window in the house ___ locked at night.
quests.hint: 'Every' always treats its noun as one at a time, no matter how many windows there are in total.
quests.explanation: 'Every window' is grammatically singular, even though the house has many windows. The verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Every applicant ___ to submit two references.
quests.hint: Think of 'every applicant' as one applicant considered individually.
quests.explanation: 'Every applicant' is singular, so it needs the -s form: 'needs'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Every seat in the theater ___ taken for tonight's show.
quests.hint: 'Every seat' considers one seat at a time, even in a full theater.
quests.explanation: 'Every seat' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb

quests.question: Each of the students ___ required to submit a project.
quests.hint: 'Each of' is always followed by a plural noun, but the subject is still 'each' - one at a time.
quests.explanation: Even though 'the students' is plural, the real subject is 'each', which is always singular. The verb agrees with 'each': 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb

quests.question: Each of the rooms ___ its own thermostat.
quests.hint: Don't be fooled by the plural noun after 'of' - the subject is still 'each'.
quests.explanation: 'Each of the rooms' is singular in meaning, since 'each' picks out one room at a time. The verb takes 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb

quests.question: Each of the answers ___ carefully checked before submission.
quests.hint: 'Each of the answers' still means one answer at a time - keep the verb singular.
quests.explanation: The subject 'each' is singular, regardless of the plural noun 'the answers' that follows 'of'. The verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase still takes a singular verb

quests.question: Every one of the packages ___ inspected before shipping.
quests.hint: 'Every one of' (as two words) works just like 'each of' - it's still singular.
quests.explanation: 'Every one of the packages' means one package at a time, so the subject is singular. The verb agrees: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every one of' + plural noun phrase takes a singular verb

quests.question: Every one of his arguments ___ a valid point.
quests.hint: Even though 'his arguments' is plural, 'every one of' still narrows it down to one at a time.
quests.explanation: 'Every one of his arguments' is singular in meaning, so the verb takes -s: 'makes'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every one of' + plural noun phrase takes a singular verb

quests.question: Every one of the workers ___ new safety training this month.
quests.hint: Notice the space between 'every' and 'one' - this two-word phrase still takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'Every one of the workers' is singular, since it considers one worker at a time. The verb takes -s: 'needs'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every one of' + plural noun phrase takes a singular verb

quests.question: Either restaurant ___ fine for tonight's dinner.
quests.hint: 'Either' refers to one of two choices, so it's always singular.
quests.explanation: 'Either restaurant' means one of the two restaurants, so the subject is singular. The verb agrees: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either' / 'either of' takes a singular verb

quests.question: Either of these routes ___ you to the airport.
quests.hint: Even with a plural noun after 'of', 'either' still refers to just one option.
quests.explanation: 'Either of these routes' means one of the two routes, so the subject stays singular. The verb takes -s: 'takes'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either' / 'either of' takes a singular verb

quests.question: Either answer ___ acceptable on the test.
quests.hint: 'Either answer' picks out one of two possible answers - treat it as singular.
quests.explanation: 'Either answer' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either' / 'either of' takes a singular verb

quests.question: Neither option ___ practical right now.
quests.hint: 'Neither' means 'not one of the two', which is still a singular idea.
quests.explanation: 'Neither option' refers to a single outcome (not one of the two), so it's treated as singular. The verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither' / 'neither of' takes a singular verb

quests.question: Neither of the applicants ___ enough experience for this role.
quests.hint: Just like 'either of', 'neither of' is followed by a plural noun but stays singular itself.
quests.explanation: 'Neither of the applicants' is singular, since it means 'not one of the two'. The verb takes 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither' / 'neither of' takes a singular verb

quests.question: Neither answer ___ correct.
quests.hint: 'Neither answer' rules out both options individually, which is still a singular idea.
quests.explanation: 'Neither answer' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither' / 'neither of' takes a singular verb

quests.question: The two brothers each ___ their own business.
quests.hint: Here 'each' comes after the subject instead of before a noun - check what the real subject is.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'the two brothers', which is plural; 'each' just adds emphasis after it. Plural subjects take the base form: 'run'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' placed after a plural subject does not change the subject's number

quests.question: My colleagues each ___ a different approach to the project.
quests.hint: 'Each' isn't attached to a noun here - the subject came before it, so check that instead.
quests.explanation: 'My colleagues' is the plural subject; 'each' afterward doesn't turn it singular. Plural subjects take 'have'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' placed after a plural subject does not change the subject's number

quests.question: The three finalists each ___ a chance to present their idea.
quests.hint: Compare this to earlier questions where 'each' came first - here it comes after the subject instead.
quests.explanation: 'The three finalists' is plural, and 'each' following it doesn't change that. The verb takes the base form: 'get'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' placed after a plural subject does not change the subject's number

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Every store on this street ___ closed by 9 PM.
quests.hint: Bring back the 'every + singular noun' rule, even with a phrase describing location.
quests.explanation: 'Every store' is singular; 'on this street' is just extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every' + singular noun takes a singular verb, even with an interrupting phrase

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Each of the doors in this building ___ a keycard lock.
quests.hint: Combine two skills here: the 'each of' rule and ignoring the interrupting phrase.
quests.explanation: 'Each of the doors' is singular, and 'in this building' doesn't change that. The verb takes 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each of' + plural noun phrase takes a singular verb, even with an interrupting phrase

quests.instruction: MATCH THE SUBJECT TO THE VERB
quests.question: Every one of the answers on the first page ___ correct.
quests.hint: Even with an extra phrase added, 'every one of' still points to a singular subject.
quests.explanation: 'Every one of the answers' is singular, and 'on the first page' is just added detail. The verb takes -s: 'looks'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Every one of' + plural noun phrase takes a singular verb, even with an interrupting phrase

quests.question: Each of the students in my advanced literature class ___ a research paper due Friday.
quests.hint: This subject is longer, but the core distributive rule hasn't changed - find 'each of' and treat it as singular.
quests.explanation: 'Each of the students' is singular, no matter how much description ('in my advanced literature class') comes after it. The verb takes 'has'.
quests.grammarRule: Distributive determiner + plural noun phrase stays singular, even with a long interrupting phrase

quests.question: Neither of the two proposals submitted by the committee ___ complete.
quests.hint: Trace past the long description of the proposals and apply the 'neither of' rule.
quests.explanation: 'Neither of the two proposals' is singular; 'submitted by the committee' is just extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: Distributive determiner + plural noun phrase stays singular, even with a long interrupting phrase

quests.question: Every one of the machines currently running on the factory floor ___ regular maintenance.
quests.hint: Even with a long description in between, 'every one of' still narrows the subject to one at a time.
quests.explanation: 'Every one of the machines' is singular; 'currently running on the factory floor' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'needs'.
quests.grammarRule: Distributive determiner + plural noun phrase stays singular, even with a long interrupting phrase

quests.question: Either of the two flights ___ available for booking today.
quests.hint: Review the 'either of' rule from earlier in this stage.
quests.explanation: 'Either of the two flights' is singular, since it refers to one of the two. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either of' + plural noun phrase takes a singular verb

quests.question: The employees each ___ their own laptop for remote work.
quests.hint: Remember the contrast: 'each' after the subject doesn't make it singular.
quests.explanation: 'The employees' is the plural subject; 'each' afterward is just an adjunct. Plural subjects take 'have'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Each' placed after a plural subject does not change the subject's number

quests.question: Neither of the witnesses ___ certain about what happened.
quests.hint: As a final check, apply the 'neither of' rule one more time.
quests.explanation: 'Neither of the witnesses' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither of' + plural noun phrase takes a singular verb
